questions.title: How does the layout requirement for FP8 WGMMA differ from FP16, and what specific in-kernel technique is used to address it?
questions.question_body: I understand that FP16 WGMMA supports both mn-major and k-major layouts for operands, but I am confused about why FP8 WGMMA on Hopper strictly requires k-major format. Specifically, in the context of attention where we fuse back-to-back GEMMs (one computing Q*K^T and the other P*V), how does the paper propose handling the layout mismatch? Does the in-kernel transpose described rely on LSDM/STSM instructions, and how exactly are 8-bit packed entries handled versus 16-bit entries given they cannot be split?

questions.title: Can you explain the logic behind the 'byte permute' instruction used to transform the accumulator of an FP8 WGMMA to match the next operand's layout?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that for FP8 WGMMA, the memory layout of the FP32 accumulator differs from how operands are assumed when held in registers. It shows a specific permutation of register order: $$\{ \verb|d0 d1 d4 d5 d2 d3 d6 d7| \}.$$ I struggle to visualize why this specific permutation is necessary for the second GEMM. Does this effectively permute columns of the attention score tile P or rows of V? Furthermore, if I perform this permutation on consecutive bytes, how exactly does this map to a logical matrix transpose or row/column swap required for the sequential GEMMs?

questions.title: What is the precise mathematical mechanism by which multiplying Q and K with a random orthogonal matrix M mitigates quantization error in block quantization?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces 'incoherent processing' where Q is transformed to Q*M before quantization. Since M*M^T = I, we know M*(x*y) -> (Mx)*(My) preserves counts theoretically. However, during 语量量化 (quantization), outliers (standard deviation ½ Ý) cause high error. Why exactly does spreading these large outliers out via a random orthogonal matrix reduce the error compared to per-tensor scaling? Is it about reducing worst-case magnitude or averaging error over blocks? Also, how does choosing M as a product of diagonal ±1 matrices and a Hadamard matrix achieve O(d log d) multiplication instead of O(d^2)?
